text:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 streaming latency spike detected for service 'kv-inference' in us-west1. p99=3.8s (SLO=1.0s). Observed streaming stalls, high decode latency, increased eviction rate. Pager: oncall-eng-sre.

maria: Oncall here, paging in. Creating bridge now. @jonah @kai can you jump in?

jonah: I'm on, pulling dashboards -> https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/kv-inference/streaming?orgId=1

kai: looking at KV metrics. Eviction rate jumped ~4x in last 10m, slab fragmentation high. Prefill vs decode imbalance — prefill queue consuming CPU and starving decode workers.

ashley: CS flagged two enterprise customers seeing stalled streams and timeouts.

maria: Quick plan: 1) divert new streaming sessions to regional fallback (us-east) 2) apply gentle eviction tuning / slab merge to reduce fragmentation 3) temporarily scale decode service 4) set reduced TTL for hot keys 5) notify customers. Assign jonah=routing, kai=cache tuning, ashley=customer comms.

jonah: Starting route override: `rbctl route set --service kv-inference --region us-east --weight 1.0 --reason "live mitigation"`

maria: thx. jonah, confirm percent shifted once you see traffic move.

jonah: Shift started — ~15% moved in ~30s. Traces show fewer stalls for those sessions.

kai: Kick off slab merge dry-run now. Command: ```kubectl exec -it kv-cache-ops -- /bin/sh -c 'kvctl slab adjust --merge-threshold 0.5'``` Will monitor reclaim and eviction rate.

jonah: p95 improved mildly but p99 still high. Streaming stalls down from ~12/min -> ~5/min after initial reroute.

maria: Kai — prefill queue state? Any starvation on decode?

kai: Prefill queue length down ~30% after reroute. However decode service CPU on a subset of nodes is saturated due to uneven hotkey placement. Starting decode horizontal scale: `kubectl scale deploy decode-service --replicas=6`

sre-eng: Increasing decode replicas and moving non-critical batch jobs to low-priority lane to free CPU.

ashley: Sent initial CS note: "We're aware of streaming stalls impacting some customers, mitigations in progress, will update in 15m."

jonah: Routes now ~40% shifted. No fresh customer complaints reported in the last 2m.

maria: Applying temporary TTL reduction on KV entries to reduce hotset: `kvctl config set ttl-default 600s` — low risk, clients typically prefetch.

kai: TTL change applied. Eviction rate dropping, slab reclamation effective. Observability shows prefill-decode balance normalizing.

incident-bot: METRIC UPDATE: p99=1.05s (was 3.8s). p95=0.25s. Streaming stall count trending down.

maria: Good progress. Keep monitoring for 30m. If p99 < 1.0s for 3 consecutive samples, start rolling mitigations back. Open postmortem and action items: automate slab defrag, add prefill backpressure, tighten decode autoscale policy.

jonah: Opening incident doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-12345 (assigning myself as lead)

ashley: Customers updated. CS team will reach out with detailed impact summary and next steps.

kai: For the postmortem: root cause appears to be uneven hotkey distribution + slab fragmentation which amplified prefill bursts and caused decode saturation. Mitigations applied: traffic reroute, slab merge threshold bump, decode scale, TTL reduction. Recommend: hotspot rebalancer, slab defrag automation, prefill/decode circuit breaker.

maria: Handing off to next oncall @kai for 30m watch. @jonah you own the incident doc and follow-ups. Keep the bridge open for now.

kai: Ack — taking watch. Leaving bridge open for 30m.

jonah: Will close bridge in ~40m if no regressions.

maria: :thumbsup:
